title: 15-Minute No-Jumping (Low Impact) Workout at Home
intro: This 15-minute routine has no jumping at all, so it's kinder on the knees and won't annoy your neighbours in a condo or flat. It still gets your heart working and your muscles tired in a controlled way.
muscles: Full body: legs, butt, chest, arms, shoulders and core, plus heart stamina.
steps: Warm up for 2 minutes: march on the spot while swinging your arms and rolling your shoulders.
Squat to chair: slowly sit down until your butt touches the chair, then stand back up. 40 seconds, rest 20 seconds.
Incline push-up: hands on a table or wall, bend your elbows and push back up. 40 seconds, rest 20 seconds.
Step back: step one leg back only halfway, return, then switch legs. Hold a chair if needed. 40 seconds, rest 20 seconds.
Standing knee drive: lift your knees towards your hands, alternating, at a comfortable pace. 40 seconds, rest 20 seconds.
Repeat steps 2-5 for 3 rounds, then cool down for 1 minute with slow walking and light stretches.
mistakes: Dropping your butt onto the chair during squats. Lower down slowly and with control.
Chasing speed until your form breaks down. It's better to do fewer reps with proper form.
Skipping the warm-up to save time. Those 2 minutes help get your joints ready.
easier: Do only 2 rounds and switch to 30 seconds work, 30 seconds rest. Do push-ups against the wall, and very small step backs while holding a chair.
harder: Increase to 4 rounds, or 45 seconds work and 15 seconds rest. Squat without touching the chair (still only halfway down), and do push-ups on a lower surface.
dose: 1 session of 15 minutes, 3 times a week for beginners, with a rest day in between. On other days, try a light walk.
safety: Stop if you feel sharp joint pain, chest pain or dizziness. If you have knee or back pain, or are recovering from an injury, do the easier version and get advice from a doctor or physiotherapist first.

faq.q: Can a no-jumping workout burn fat?
faq.a: Yes, it still uses energy and helps if you're consistent. But fat loss comes from your overall eating and movement, not from one type of exercise alone.

faq.q: Can I do it every day?
faq.a: You can if your body feels okay, but for beginners, 3 times a week with rest days or walking in between is easier to keep up.

faq.q: When is the best time to do it?
faq.a: Whenever you can actually do it. Some like the morning before work, some after the kids are asleep. Avoid doing it right after a heavy meal.
